  B.  Proposed Budget for Fiscal Year 2024-25

  Recommended Action: Provide a recommendation to the City Council regarding
  the Fiscal Year (FY) 2024-25 Proposed Budget.

  Assistant City Manager Toney provided a presentation on the proposed budget. As
  recommended by the City Council he added items surrounding speed cameras,
  rental rates for facility use, Wi-Fi at the parks, and the feasibility of adding a dog
  park at Las Flores Park. He added that there was a previous discussion regarding a
  dog park and the information has been added to the agenda report. He stated that it
  was reviewed in 2021 and presented to the Parks and Recreation Commission and
  it was recommended not to move forward at the Las Flores location, vacant lands
  were proposed, due to ESHA limitations, parking, and size of the location.

  Councilmember Silverstein inquired if any public beaches allowed dogs on the
  beach, and inquired if the city could pursue the possibility of designating a Malibu
  beach as a dog beach.

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated that this has been done in other areas such as
  the City of Long Beach and Santa Barbara County.

  City Manager McClary added that Malibu will need to inquire with both the county
  and the state as there are beaches owned by both jurisdictions.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart spoke about the facility use rental rates, he stated that the
  marathon and triathlon are on county parking property and Malibu spends money
  to support this.

  Finance Manager Neermann clarified that the agencies who oversee the marathon
  and triathlon cover the Sheriff’s fees.

  City Manager McClary explained that most of the impact has been on the
  administration side of the agreement and is unsure of the impact on the day-to-day,
  the Community Services Department staff, or other staff.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart stated that the city should aim to recover funds where
  possible. He added that regarding speed cameras, the figure wouldn’t have to be
  specific, and an estimated allocation would suffice as a placeholder.

  Assistant City Manager Toney explained that there are multiple ways of
  appropriating funds, either upfront or throughout the fiscal year.

  In response to Assistant City Manager Toney, Mayor Pro Tem Stewart stated that
  his goal is to ensure that there is an expedited process when it comes to the speed
  camera project.

  City Manager McClary stated that it is best to come up with a placeholder value
  because Senator Ben Allen's office is requesting an estimated figure for the
  appropriations committee.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart recommended gathering that estimated figure based on
  nine cameras. He also inquired about the funding process for funding projects that
  may come out of surveys.

  Finance Manager Neermann explained that this could also be funded while the
  request for proposals and contracts are being finalized.

  Councilmember Silverstein inquired about Los Angeles County Sheriff and
  California Highway Patrol coverage overnight between 10 pm to 5 am.

  City Manager McClary stated that nighttime coverage is sparse in comparison to
  daytime coverage.

  Councilmember Silverstein recommended allocating resources for nighttime
  coverage to patrol nighttime speeding.

  City Manager McClary recommended meeting with Captain Seetoo to further
  discuss resource allocation and any challenges they may have. He stated that CHP
  is also limited to assignments.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart said that patrol assignments are based on availability and
  should be accepting the help they can get. He highlighted an issue of overtime
  versus dedicated officers and added that the officers are doing the best they can. He
  explained that a discussion with Captain Seetoo would be beneficial. He also stated
  that there would be a second request to use funds for the Malibu Education Fund
  and inquired if a line item should be added at that time.

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated that the Administration and Finance
  Subcommittee can make a recommendation to the City Council to set aside funds
  to be included as a line item in the budget as an appropriation, however, they would
  still need to submit a request for those funds.

  Councilmember Silverstein recommended that they make a formal request first
  before any funds get allocated.

  Assistant City Manager Toney continued his presentation and explained that there
  are currently Prop A funds totaling about $1.1 million. He stated that these funds
  are limited to transportation services and if they are left unused, they are lost. He

  added that another city is interested in purchasing those funds for a discount. He
  explained that transportation services in the city are limited and include items such
  as Dial a Ride.

  Councilmember Silverstein posed several questions to staff.

  Finance Manager Neermann stated that this was most recently done in 2019. She
  added that Prop A funds are distributed to the city each year and selling the funds
  at a discount this year will not impact future year’s funds. She added that these
  funds have very specific uses such as building a bus stop and explained that it
  cannot be used for parking-related items.

  Councilmember Silverstein asked if the funds could be used for school
  transportation for kids.

  City Manager McClary stated that spending the money will require staff time to
  complete the projects.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart stated that the funds were to be used or lost and inquired
  if the discount was market rate.

  Finance Manager Neermann stated that only one city was interested in purchasing
  those funds for a discount.

  Councilmember Silverstein agreed that he would be okay with selling the funds this
  year as long as the funds returned are general funds and future Prop A funds are not
  impacted by this transaction.

  Assistant City Manager Toney explained that this current year's transaction can be
  executed at the City Manager level. He explained that there are multiple reasons to
  increase the CIP budget; one of those being the permanent skatepark, which was
  originally estimated at $1.1 million and is now estimated closer to $2.5 million
  within the next fiscal year.

  City Manager McClary added that there were prior discussions at the Parks and
  Recreation Commission regarding fundraising or sponsorship opportunities and
  discussions were shifted towards the city funding this project.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart recommended having further discussions regarding
  naming rights at the City Council level.

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated that a public hearing will be held on May 28th
  and the budget is scheduled to be adopted at the end of June. He reviewed the status
  of revenues and expenditures and added that they are structurally balanced for the
  most part. He continued with his presentation to introduce proposed staffing
  changes including several new positions, a 3.4% cost of living adjustment, and

  completion of the classification and compensation study. He continued to review
  each department's budget changes. He also touched on the Baker Tilly report and
  reported that they have made headway on culture and retention and are still making
  improvements across all 46 recommendations. He added that three main
  recommendations included establishing a Community Development Department; it
  was recommended to add a placeholder for a Community Development Director.
  He explained that most cities do not have separate Planning and Building
  Departments. He stated that this would need to be researched further and returned
  to the City Council with the options and analysis, and this would be a placeholder
  for a position for future leeway.

  City Manager McClary stated that the most modern option is to have a unified
  department, as he has not seen many cities lead towards separating departments.

  Councilmember Silverstein inquired if the Baker Tilly Report was a receive and file
  only.

  Assistant City Manager Toney explained that the findings were presented to the
  City Council for feedback, and provided to the City Manager for implementation.
  He added that there were both short-term and long-term solutions.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart recommended that an item be brought to the City Council
  to provide a progress report on implementation.

  Councilmember Silverstein commended staff for the great budget presentation at
  the last City Council meeting. He inquired about the Sheriff's Department
  allocations.

  Assistant City Manager Toney explained at a high level how the services are
  allocated and explained that it would be more expensive to have a Police
  Department or Fire Department.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart, requested more details when it came to the pie charts for
  example Management Administration Services Department to include information
  on IT, Human Resources, or Media.
  Assistant City Manager Toney shared that a further breakdown of divisions can be
  found on page 11 of the budget and that additional slides can be added to the
  presentation.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart stated that he would leave that decision up to staff but
  would like to see further breakdowns to ensure confidence in incoming income;
  including confidence levels.

  City Manager McClary stated that although currently, the city is on an upward
  trend, those assumptions cannot be made each year.

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated that property taxes swing but historically they
  have been at six percent. He added that inelasticity was the reason why most
  organizations such as schools are based on property taxes. He added that hotel and
  private have leveled off within the past two years, between 9 – 10 million.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart inquired if there was a process to track TOT payments to
  ensure full compliance.

  Finance Manager Neermann stated that the city is doing everything possible and
  has a consultant who scans websites and spot-checks individual locations to ensure
  compliance.

  Assistant City Manager Toney explained that when the budget was developed, the
  department was going off the current year quarter two for the estimates. He stated
  that the finance team will be going back to those estimates for revenue and
  expenses.

  City Manager McClary stated that as a follow-up to the budget workshop he has
  tasked the Community Services Department to draft a policy on city land and
  facility rentals.

  Councilmember Silverstein encouraged staff to have different rates for non-profit
  agencies.

  to recommend to the City Council to adopt recommendations of staff subject to
  feedback.

Subject:  Fiscal Year 2023-24 Third Quarter Financial Report

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Review Fiscal Year (FY) 2023-24 Third Quarter Financial
Report.

FISCAL IMPACT: There is no fiscal impact associated with the recommended action. As
of March 31, 2024, the projected General Fund Undesignated Reserve at June 30, 2024,
is $73.37 million.

DISCUSSION: The attached report provides revenue, expenditure and fund balance
totals for the third quarter of FY 2023-24

The Revenues by Fund Report (pages A 1-5) reflects General Fund revenues received
of $34.3 million or 58.9% of the amended budgeted amount for the fiscal year. Total
revenue for all funds received through the third quarter is $42.5 million or 51.1% of the
amended budgeted amount for the fiscal year. Many revenue sources are received on a
quarterly or annual basis creating a lag in receipt, and as such, will be reflected when the
year-end report is presented. For example, property taxes are remitted by the County
after they are paid by property owners in December and April; Property Tax – In Lieu
payments typically come at the end of the year; and Transient Occupancy Tax – Private
Rentals is remitted quarterly. Sales Tax is remitted quarterly to the State and then
passed along to the City.

The Expenditure by Fund Report (pages A 6-9) reflects any budget carryovers from FY
2022-23, as well as the appropriations approved by the City Council for the current fiscal
year in the Amended Budget column. Budget Adjustments, Carryovers and Council

  Agenda Item #3.B.
 Appropriations total $4.6 million as of March 31, 2024. General Fund expenditures for
the third quarter total $31.4 million or 43.3% of the amended budget. Expenditures for all
funds total $39.1 million or 40.0% of the amended budget.

Projected Fund Balances for the fiscal year end are reflected on page A-10. The
projected Undesignated Fund Balance at June 30, 2024, includes all expenses
appropriated as of March 31, 2024 by the Council. The City ended FY 2022-23 with
$61.5 million in the Undesignated General Fund Reserve. As of March 31, 2024, the
projected General Fund Undesignated Reserve at June 30, 2024, is $73.4 million. In
addition, there is $6.5 million in Contingency that is available at the discretion of the
Council.

Third Quarter Budget Amendments
The Revenue and Expenditure amendments for this period are corrections and detailed
on pages A-5 and A-9 respectively.

The only adjustment for Q3 pertains to Proposition A Local Return (Prop A) funds. The
City has Prop A funds that could potentially lapse if we do not use them. This is due to
the low level of transportation programming in the City. While the City offers Dial-a-Ride
and Community Transportation programming, the estimated year end expenditures from
these funds are only about $161,000 in FY 2023-24, with a projected fund balance of
$1.24 million. To not lose the Prop A benefit, the City is able to exchange the funds to
another city at a discount. Staff have negotiated exchanging the funds at $0.73 on the
dollar, and the subsequent sale results in General Fund dollars. The City will exchange
about $450,000 from the Prop A Fund Balance and will receive an estimated $328,500 in
General Fund in return, a net financial impact of -$121,500, to the Fund Balance on All
Funds. This is displayed in the FY 2023-24 Estimated revenue and expenditures and in
the Fund Balance at June 30, 2024. The Estimated expenditures are modified in Object
3009-Transportation Services from $161,000 to $611,000, and the revenues are
modified from in Object 3602-Proposition A Transportation Funds Exchange.

The FY 2023-24 Third Quarter Financial Report will be presented to the City Council on
June 10, 2024.

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Stewart seconded a motion

  B. Fiscal Year 2023-24 Third Quarter Financial Report

  Recommended Action: Review Fiscal Year (FY) 2023-24 Third Quarter Financial
  Report.

  Assistant City Manager Toney presented the staff report. He provided a high-level
  summary which included revenues and expenditures. He stated that the third quarter
  is similar to the third quarter of the previous year.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart inquired about property taxes.

  Assistant City Manager Toney clarified that projecting property tax payments are
  not split in half and explained that one payment is larger than the other and other
  smaller payment disbursements.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart inquired about the FEMA reimbursement.

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated that the process could take longer than
  expected and depends on how proj ects are closed.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart inquired about the interest earnings, wastewater, and park
  development totals.

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated that he would follow up on getting an answer
  regarding these totals.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart inquired about the available SCE funds.

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated that those funds are still tied to some proj ects
  and shared that they can get additional information on how these funds were
  allocated.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart inquired about the budget for Public Safety.

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated that a large portion of those funds are for the
  Sheriff Substation, however, added that hiring has been difficult, and they have
  lowered those appropriations for the upcoming fiscal year.

  Councilmember Silverstein inquired about personnel being a line item and inquired
  if it could be added to the quarterly reports.

  Finance Manager Neermann stated that personnel is a line item in the budget, and
  shared that personnel could be added as a separate schedule in the quarterly reports

  as a total. She stated that it would take effort to include this information for each
  department, but the department would do what they can.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart inquired about capital project spending.

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated that some of the lack of spending is due to
  multi-year projects getting full allocation.

  Finance Manager Neermann agreed and shared that they have spoken with the
  departments and have asked them to only add to the budget what is anticipated for
  the one year instead of allocating the funds for a multiyear project.

  City Manager McClary shared that in working with neighboring cities he has
  learned that this is a common issue amongst other cities. He stated that there is also
  a built-in lag where payments aren’t paid until later in the fiscal year.

  Assistant City Manager Toney reiterated the importance of a 5-year plan for capital
  improvement plans and grant funding.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart inquired about the Legacy Park debt service.

  Finance Manager Neermann stated that the city receives a one-time annual invoice.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart inquired about surplus funds.

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated that there are many reasons, including a lack
  of staffing and creating better department projections.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart commended the finance team for all their hard work.

ADJOURNMENT

  At 3:11 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Stewart adjourned the meeting.
